description: Responsive card grid for discrete content objects — posts, features, team members, process steps. Not for decorative icon grids. Cards are 1-col mobile, 2-col tablet, 3-col desktop unless `columns` says otherwise. REBUILT ON THE UNIVERSAL DESIGN CONTRACT (v2): it declares no style slots. Every designable value — colour, type, spacing, border, shadow, size, motion — is set through the `udc` map on the band, per role. It is also the FIRST component to declare `item_roles`, so a single card can carry its own `udc` map and be styled on its own (BUILD-SPEC Addendum B). See docs/v2/BUILD-SPEC-sprint0.md §3 and Addendum B.

id.description: Optional HTML id attribute for anchor linking (e.g. navigation anchors).

title.description: Section heading above the grid. Omit if the context makes it clear. Plain text — HTML is escaped.

title_accent.description: Optional exact substring of title to render in an accent color. Must match title exactly (case-sensitive) or it is ignored.

eyebrow.description: Optional short kicker/label rendered as a pill above the title. Plain text — HTML is escaped.

subheading.description: Optional supporting line below the title. Plain text — HTML is escaped.

layout.description: Structural layout. 'cards' = standard card grid. 'steps' = numbered process cards, each carrying a filled circular number badge above its title. Use 'steps' for How-it-works / process flows. This is STRUCTURE, not styling: it changes which elements render (the badge, and no card images), so it stays a prop. The badge's look is the `step-number` role.

columns.description: Optional explicit desktop (>=768px) column count, an integer 1-4. Unset (key absent, null, or empty) keeps the default auto-derivation from item count. When set it forces that many equal-width columns at >=768px, spanning the container; the single-column collapse below 768px is unchanged. Out-of-range or non-integer values (0, 5, 2.5, text) are rejected, not clamped. Cards-layout concept; ignored on 'steps', which keeps its fixed process grain. Track geometry is structure, so this stays a prop — the same reason hero kept `split_ratio`. For a per-breakpoint count, the `list` role's `layout.columns` is the UDC route.

items.description: Array of card items. Each: { title, text, bullets, image_url, image_alt, image_id, link_url, link_text }. When layout is 'steps', also include: { number }. A single card may ALSO carry its own `udc` map to style just that card — see `item_roles` and BUILD-SPEC Addendum B. The `udc` and `id` keys on an entry are engine-owned and are not listed as fields here: `id` is minted on write and must not be authored, and `udc` is a design map rather than content.

number.description: Step number label (e.g. '1', '01', '1.'). Required when grid layout is 'steps'.

title.description: Card heading. Plain text — HTML is escaped.

text.description: Card body / supporting text. Inline HTML allowed: a, strong, em, br.

bullets.description: Optional checklist lines rendered below text, each prefixed with a check mark. Plain text only — no HTML/markdown; each line is escaped independently. Use for scannable feature/benefit lists instead of cramming items into one text sentence.

image_alt.description: Alt text for the card image. Leave empty only if the image is purely decorative.

image_id.description: Media Library attachment ID (NOT a URL). When it resolves to a real attachment, the image renders responsively with srcset/sizes via wp_get_attachment_image() instead of a single fixed-size . Falls back to image_url when unset or unresolvable. Get an attachment id via the import_media apply.

link_url.description: Optional card link destination. Accepts an absolute URL, a site-relative /path, an #anchor, mailto:, or tel:; a disallowed protocol (javascript:, data:) is rejected at write time.

item_roles._note: BUILD-SPEC Addendum B5. Which of this component's roles a SINGLE items[] entry may address through its own `udc` map, and which prop holds the repeater. The engine reads this declaration and holds no list of component names, so any repeater component can declare the same thing. `root` is the role whose element carries the minted `data-pp-item` attribute. The band-level header roles (_band, header, eyebrow, heading, heading-accent, subheading, list, empty) are deliberately absent: they exist once per band, so styling them 'for one card' has no meaning.

retired_props._note: Props this component declared on 1.x that the v2 rebuild retired (#1101). Each value names the v2 surface that replaced it, so a refusal can offer a route instead of a list of live prop names. Guarded by SchemaValidationTest, which fails in BOTH directions: a key here that still exists in props, or a route naming a role this component does not declare, is a test failure rather than a message that lies.
retired_props.theme: the `_band` role — and it takes MORE than a background, which is why the route names several roles rather than one. MEASURED in Chromium at 375/768/1280, all three values, before the prop went: `default` painted NO background at all (transparent) with no border; `muted` painted `@color-surface` plus a 1px solid `@color-border` rule top and bottom (it emitted the legacy `grid--dark` class, #570 DG-4); `inverted` painted `@color-bg-inverted`, re-coloured the heading to `@color-bg` and the subheading to `@color-bg`, and left the CARDS light — measured, card fill, title, text, bullets and link were byte-identical on a `default` and an `inverted` band, because v1 deliberately kept cards light on a dark band. So: the tone is `_band` -> `background.fill`; the `muted` framing is `border.width-top`/`width-bottom` = "1px" with `style-top`/`style-bottom` = "solid" and `color` = "@color-border"; the `inverted` ink is `typography.color` on `_band`, which the `heading` role follows through `currentColor`. THE SUBHEADING DOES NOT FOLLOW and needs its own write — see that role. `dark` was not an accepted input value: it was removed at #605 and `pp_theme_class()` clamped it to `default`.
retired_props.title_align: the `header` role — `typography.align` for the text, which the eyebrow pill and the heading both follow, the pill because an inline-block is an inline-level box and text alignment moves it. MEASURED before the route was written: v1's `center` value set `text-align: center` on `.grid__header` and ALSO added `margin-left`/`margin-right: auto` to the header, the heading and the subheading, which centres each capped BOX as well as its text. Only the heading's cap (`@measure-heading`) and the subheading's 40rem ever bind, so the box half is visible only on short copy; it is `spacing.margin-left`/`margin-right` = "auto" on those two roles, which the spacing group accepts as a keyword. Two writes instead of one prop, and both are ordinary role parameters — no grammar changed.
retired_props.card_emphasis: the `card`, `card-bar`, `card-title` and `card-body` roles on a SINGLE item, through that item's own `udc` map (Addendum B). RETIRED RATHER THAN PORTED, and the reason is the contract rather than convenience: v1's `featured` treatment was `:first-child`, which is ORDINAL styling, and Addendum B exclusion 3 rules that an item is addressed by its minted id and nothing else so that reordering carries styling WITH the item. Keeping an ordinal treatment beside an id-addressed one would leave two systems disagreeing about which card is special the moment a list is reordered. MEASURED ON THE OWNER'S LIVE SITE before retiring it: all 11 production grid bands render `grid--uniform`, i.e. the featured treatment was already switched off everywhere it could have applied.
retired_props.image_treatment: the `card-media` role — `sizing.aspect-ratio` plus `sizing.width`/`sizing.height` for the box. v1's `icon` value rendered a 48x48 un-cropped box instead of the 16:9 cover banner; in v2 that is `card-media` -> `sizing` -> `{"width": "48px", "height": "48px", "aspect-ratio": "auto"}`. THE UN-CROPPED FIT IS A STATED NARROWING: `object-fit` has no typed parameter in the Sizing group, so the `contain` half of the icon treatment is reachable only through the raw-CSS valve, `card-media` -> `_css` -> `{"object-fit": "contain"}`. Measured live exposure of `image_treatment` before retiring it: ZERO bands and zero card images across all 11 production grid bands.
retired_props.items[].text_role: the `card-text` role's own `udc` map on that item (Addendum B), or a custom preset (#1016). v1's four values were mono/meta/label/kicker. MEASURED, all four, at desktop: `mono` and `meta` rendered byte-identically to the default body text — the premium typography tier's own `.grid__item-text` rule out-ranked both presets, so two of the four values had NO rendered effect at all and the schema's claim that meta and kicker 'also set a preset text color' was false at every viewport above 767px. Only `label` (letter-spacing 0.01em) and `kicker` (letter-spacing 0.08em + uppercase) changed anything. Per-item typography is exactly what an item `udc` map expresses, so the capability is wider after the retirement than before it.
retired_props.items[].style: the entry's own `udc` map (Addendum B1), addressing the SAME roles the component declares — `card` for the panel itself, `card-bar`, `card-media`, `card-body`, `card-title`, `card-text`, `card-bullets`, `card-bullet`, `card-link` and `step-number` for its parts (see `item_roles`). v1 accepted 21 card-scoped slot names here and rendered them as INLINE custom properties on that card's `.grid__item`; §3.4 forbids inline style emission outright, so the replacement is `{"udc": {"card": {"background": {"fill": "#14141F"}}, "card-title": {"typography": {"color": "#F2EEE5"}}}}` on the entry, which emits `[data-pp-band="…"] [data-pp-item="…"]` rules instead. This is the capability Addendum B exists for, and it is WIDER than the slot map was: same engine, same grammar, same refusal codes as a band map, and the id the engine mints means the design travels with the card rather than with its position.

_band.description: The band itself — the <section>. Set the band's own background here to make a dark or tinted band; the v1 `theme` prop is gone because a preset bundle of colours is exactly what the UDC expresses directly. THE DEFAULTS ARE WHAT v1's UNTHEMED BAND RENDERED, measured in Chromium at 375/768/1280 rather than read off the stylesheet: the shared band rhythm and NOTHING ELSE. v1's `.grid` declared `background: transparent` and no border on any edge, so silence here is the faithful port — the framing rules belonged to `.grid--dark`, the retired `theme: "muted"` variant. A band background image is `background.image` (an attachment id) with `background.overlay` for the scrim. SETTING `typography.color` HERE RE-INKS THE HEADING AND NOTHING ELSE ON THIS COMPONENT. The `heading` role follows it through `currentColor`; every other text role pins a measured v1 value and a pinned role default is a DIRECT declaration that an inherited band colour can never beat. THE CARDS ARE THE REASON, and it is a design decision v1 made deliberately: on a v1 `inverted` band the cards stayed LIGHT, so `card-title`, `card-text`, `card-bullets` and `card-link` measured byte-identical on a dark band and a light one. If you darken THIS band and leave the cards alone, the cards stay light and everything in them is still legible — that is the supported shape. If you ALSO darken the cards (`card` -> `background.fill`), you own the ink inside them: set `card-title`, `card-text`, `card-bullets` and `card-link` colours in the same write. `subheading` and `empty` sit on the BAND fill, not inside a card, so a dark band strands both unless you re-ink them; `eyebrow` carries its own `@color-surface-accent` pill fill so it does not strand, and `heading-accent` on `@color-bg-inverted` measures 3.23:1, which clears the 3:1 large-text floor only because the heading clamp floors at 28px — re-ink it deliberately rather than by accident.

obligations.why: The subheading pins @color-muted, so a colour set on the band does not reach it. A dark band leaves it at 3.1:1 or worse unless you set subheading typography.color too.
The empty-state line pins @color-muted and renders on the band fill, not inside a card, so darkening the band strands it.

header.description: The eyebrow/title/subheading block above the cards. It owns the alignment of the whole header — v1's retired `title_align` prop — and nothing else: measured, it declared no padding, no margin and no background of its own at any viewport. Set `typography.align` to centre the text; the eyebrow pill is an inline-block whose BOX does not follow text alignment once the header is a flex column, so centre it with `layout.align` in the same write. IT DECLARES NO `layout` GROUP, and that is a box fact rather than an omission: `.grid__header` is an ordinary block, so `justify-content` or `align-items` on it would paint nothing at any value (the #1006 inert class). Centre the header with `typography.align` — the eyebrow pill is an inline-level box, so it follows the text alignment — and give the heading and subheading `spacing.margin-left`/`margin-right` of `auto` if you also want their capped boxes centred rather than only their text.

eyebrow.description: The kicker pill above the heading. Measured byte-identical to cta's, section's, faq's and hero's eyebrow roles, and declared per-schema rather than extracted for the reason #1023 recorded: role declaration is data the engine shares, so a fifth copy of the same values is the contract working rather than duplication to factor out. It carries its own `@color-surface-accent` fill, which is why a dark band does not strand it the way it strands `subheading`.

heading.description: The band heading (an <h2>). ITS `typography.color` IS `currentColor`, AND THAT IS A MEASURED PORT RATHER THAN A TRANSCRIPTION. v1's rule was `color: var(--grid-heading-color, var(--color-text))` — a pinned literal — but the only way v1 could render a dark grid band was `theme: "inverted"`, which supplied a light heading colour through `--pp-grid-heading-theme-color`, and that prop is retired. Measured both ways before choosing: `#101828` on a light band and `#fcfdff` on an inverted one, so a pinned literal would reproduce exactly one of the two and would pin the heading against the one band shape v2 newly makes easy. `currentColor` in the `color` property is defined to mean `inherit`, so an authored `_band` -> `typography.color` reaches this heading and an authored value on this role still wins. Identical to `@color-text` on every band v1 could actually express. ITS WEIGHT, LEADING AND RHYTHM ARE RESTATED and its family, tracking and `text-wrap` are not: the weight and leading came from `main > .grid .grid__heading` rules that existed ONLY inside media queries, so dropping them would have restyled every tier, while the other three come from base.css's shared h1-h6 rule and restating a global value would move it to the unlayered tier and beat that rule in every state. Measured letter-spacing is exactly -0.03em at all three tiers, which IS base.css's global — hence no default.

heading-accent.description: The accented substring inside the heading, rendered only when title_accent occurs in title exactly. It PINS `@color-accent` and therefore does NOT follow a band colour — on `@color-bg-inverted` that measures 3.23:1, which passes the 3:1 large-text floor only because the heading's clamp floors at 28px. It is an 80% cut in margin beside a 17.54:1 heading, so re-ink it deliberately on a dark band rather than by accident.

subheading.description: The supporting line below the heading. IT PINS `@color-muted` AND THAT IS THE MEASURED PORT, not an oversight — and it is the one role on this component where neither `currentColor` nor a pinned literal reproduces both of v1's configurations. Measured: `rgb(94,102,119)` on a light band and `#fcfdff` on a v1 `inverted` one. `currentColor` would reproduce the dark case and CHANGE the light one, which is the overwhelmingly common band; the literal reproduces every band v1 could express and strands only the band shape v2 newly makes easy. The literal wins, and the cost is recorded here and as an obligation on `_band`: darken the band and this line needs its own `typography.color` in the same write. Its size and leading come from base.css and are deliberately not restated. ITS MEASURE IS A PORTED DEFAULT, not an omission: v1 declared `max-width: 40rem` on this element at every tier (measured), the same measure section's and testimonials' subheadings carry, so it is `sizing.max-width` here rather than a literal left in the stylesheet.

obligations.why: This role pins @color-muted, so a typography.color set on the band does not reach it. Set it here too when you darken the band.

list.description: The card grid itself — the <ul>. It owns the GAP between cards and, through `layout.columns`, the track count. The track count is also settable structurally with the `columns` prop; the difference is that the prop is one number for >=768px while `layout.columns` takes a breakpoint map, so reach for the role when the phone, tablet and desktop counts differ. The measured gap is tier-variant and is a real breakpoint map rather than a token: 0.85rem / 1rem / 1.05rem.

card.description: One card — the <li>, and THE ITEM ROOT: this is the element that carries `data-pp-item` when an entry declares its own `udc` map, so an item-grain `card` write emits at `[data-pp-band="…"] [data-pp-item="…"]`. ITS FILL IS LOAD-BEARING FOR EVERY INK INSIDE IT. v1 kept cards light even on an inverted band — measured, `card-title`, `card-text`, `card-bullets` and `card-link` were byte-identical on a `default` and an `inverted` band — which is why all four pin their colours instead of following the band. THE CONSEQUENCE IS YOURS TO CARRY: if you darken this fill, whether on the band or on one item, set `card-title`, `card-text`, `card-bullets` and `card-link` colours in the SAME write, or the text keeps a dark value on a dark panel. That is exactly what the owner's production design does per card, and it is the acceptance case Addendum B exists for. `overflow: hidden` is structural — it is what clips a banner image to this box's radius — and it is also why `card-link`'s focus ring is drawn INSET rather than outset (see that role). ONE MEASURED DEFAULT CHANGED RATHER THAN PORTED, stated because it is visible: v1's fill was `linear-gradient(180deg, var(--color-bg) 0%, var(--color-surface) 100%)`, a very subtle top-to-bottom tint. The value grammar accepts a gradient of LITERALS and a bare `@token`, but not a token INSIDE a gradient — so the two ways to port it were a token-following flat fill or a hex gradient frozen against every retheme. The flat `@color-bg` wins, matching what faq's `item` and testimonials' `card` already default for the same visual job: a default that stops following the design tokens is a worse failure than a lost 2% tint, and an author who wants the tint can still write the literal gradient here.

obligations.why: The card title pins @color-text, so darkening the card fill does not re-ink it. Set card-title typography.color in the same write.
The card text pins its own colour, so darkening the card fill does not re-ink it. Set card-text typography.color in the same write.
The checklist pins @color-muted, so darkening the card fill does not re-ink it. Set card-bullets typography.color in the same write.

A colour here lands on the wrapper and reaches an <a> inside it only by inheritance, while the stylesheet gives every anchor its own direct rule. Set the paired link role named above too, and its `:hover`.

card-bar.description: The thin rule across the top of every card. IT IS A REAL ELEMENT IN v2 AND WAS A PSEUDO-ELEMENT IN v1, and that change is why the capability survived the rebuild at all. v1 painted it with `.grid__item::before`, and Addendum B6 exclusion 6 defers pseudo-elements — so ported literally, the bar's colour and height would have had no v2 address and would have retired. MEASURED ON THE OWNER'S LIVE SITE BEFORE DECIDING: 10 of his 11 production grid bands author both slots, all ten with the identical pair `linear-gradient(120deg,#7B5BFF 0%,#FF5C2E 50%,#3DDFC8 100%)` at `3px`. That is a brand signature on 91% of bands, not an unused slot, so the honest port was to give the thing its own selector — the same move `nav.link-current` and `faq.question-open` already make when the selector grammar cannot reach something. An empty <span aria-hidden="true"> costs one element per card and keeps a capability the reconstruction depends on. Measured default: `@color-border` at 2px on an ordinary card. It renders on the cards layout only; steps has no bar.

card-media.description: The card's image box. It owns the BOX; the image inside it is sized structurally to fill that box. The measured default is a 16:9 cover banner at every viewport. v1's retired `image_treatment: "icon"` is this role with `sizing` set to a small square and `aspect-ratio` cleared — see `retired_props` for the exact shape, including the one narrowing that carries: `object-fit` has no typed parameter in the Sizing group, so the un-cropped `contain` fit is reachable only through `_css`.

card-body.description: The padded content area inside a card — everything below the image. IT OWNS THE CARD'S PADDING, not the `card` role, and the split is structural rather than arbitrary: a banner image is full-bleed to the card's edges while the text is inset, so the padding cannot live on the element the image is a sibling of. Set padding here; set the card's fill, border, radius and shadow on `card`. The measured padding is tier-variant and a real breakpoint map: 1.55rem on the phone, 2rem from 768px up. It also owns the vertical rhythm between title, text, bullets and link through `spacing.gap`. IT CARRIES `typography` FOR ONE MEASURED REASON: v1's `--grid-item-text-align` set `text-align` on THIS element, and its children (title, text, bullets) are full-width flex items, so the alignment inherits into all of them from here. `typography.align` is that slot's route. The card link is the exception the #338 flex trap describes — it is a content-width flex item whose BOX text alignment cannot move, so it follows `card-link` -> `sizing.align-self` instead.

card-title.description: The card heading (an <h3>). It PINS `@color-text` and therefore does not follow a band or card colour — measured byte-identical on a v1 `default` and `inverted` band, because v1 kept cards light on a dark band. Darken the card and you must set this too. Its size, weight and leading are restated because they came from media-query-scoped rules that would otherwise have restyled every tier; the measured weight is genuinely tier-variant (660 on the phone, 670 above it), which is a real breakpoint map rather than a rounding artefact.

obligations.why: This role pins @color-text, so a typography.color set on the card does not reach it. Set it here too when you darken a card.

card-text.description: The card's supporting paragraph. ITS COLOUR IS A BREAKPOINT MAP AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT INVENTED: v1 rendered `@color-muted` below 768px and `@color-text-secondary` from 768px up, because the premium typography tier only lightened the paragraph at the wider tiers. Porting one of the two would have changed the other. Like every ink inside a card it pins rather than inherits, so darkening a card fill needs this role set in the same write.

obligations.why: This role pins its own colour, so a typography.color set on the card does not reach it. Set it here too when you darken a card.

card-bullets.description: The checklist below the card text — the <ul>. It owns the colour, type and gap of the whole list; the individual line's indent is `card-bullet`. NOTE THE MEASURED ASYMMETRY WITH `card-text`, which is a real v1 behaviour rather than an inconsistency to tidy: the bullet list has NO desktop tier of its own, so it stays `@color-muted` at every viewport while the paragraph above it lightens to `@color-text-secondary` from 768px up. Setting this role's colour is what makes the two agree. THE CHECK-MARK GLYPH'S COLOUR HAS NO v2 ADDRESS: it is painted by a pseudo-element, which Addendum B6 exclusion 6 defers, so v1's `--grid-item-bullet-color` retired with a stated narrowing — measured live exposure on the owner's site was ZERO bands. #1028 is the ruling that would give it a home.

obligations.why: This role pins @color-muted, so a typography.color set on the card does not reach it. Set it here too when you darken a card.

card-bullet.description: One checklist line. It exists as its own role for exactly one measured value: the 1.5rem left indent that makes room for the check-mark glyph. Colour, size and leading are NOT declared here — they inherit from `card-bullets`, which is where you set them, and restating them would give this role a direct declaration that beat its own container for no reason.

card-link.description: The card's 'Read more' link. It PINS `@color-accent`, which measures 3.2:1 on a `#14141F` card fill — under the 4.5:1 AA floor for its 0.9rem weight-600 text — so darkening a card means setting this colour in the same write. ITS FOCUS RING IS DRAWN INSET, AND THAT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DECORATIVE: `.grid__item` declares `overflow: hidden` to clip a banner image to the card radius, and base.css paints focus rings 2px OUTSIDE the control, so an outset ring on this link lands entirely in the clipped region and paints nothing. v1 survived that only because the card's padding happened to be wider than the 4px the ring needs; in v2 that padding is an ordinary authored value on `card-body`, so the defect was one write away (#1056). The remedy is #1046's, already proven on faq: a negative outline offset, applied structurally so no authored value can reopen it. ITS UNDERLINE IS A STATE PAIR, ported whole: base.css underlines every `a`, v1 removed it at rest and put it back on hover, and measured `text-decoration-line` read `none` at rest and `underline` on hover with `@color-accent-hover` ink. Both halves are defaults here — `typography.decoration` plus a `:hover` block — on nav `link`'s precedent, because keeping the rest half in the stylesheet would have left an authored `decoration` unable to win the hover.

obligations.why: This role pins @color-accent, which measures 3.2:1 on a dark card fill. Set it here too when you darken a card.

step-number.description: The filled circular number badge on the steps layout. Renders only when `layout` is 'steps'. Its fill and its numeral ink are a PAIR: the fill defaults to `@color-accent` and the numeral to `@color-bg`, so setting one without the other is how a light badge ends up with invisible numerals. Its measured box is tier-variant — 40px on the phone, 44px from 768px up — and the 44px is the shared tap-target floor rather than a free choice (#1058).

obligations.why: The badge pins @color-accent as its fill and @color-bg as its numeral. Changing one without the other is how a light badge gets invisible numerals.

empty.description: The line rendered when the band has no items. IT SITS ON THE BAND FILL, NOT INSIDE A CARD, which is the whole reason it needs its own mention: darkening the cards cannot strand it and re-inking the card roles cannot rescue it. It pins `@color-muted`, so a dark BAND strands it at roughly 3.1:1 unless you set this role's colour in the same write.

obligations.why: The empty-state line pins @color-muted and sits on the band fill, so a typography.color set on the band does not reach it.

do_not_touch: schema.json without updating this component's README.md and the repo-root AI_CONTEXT.md
